reasons.rubric: Set-membership on a small discount roll is simple, but the verifier barely cares and frequency is low and the issuer ecosystem is fragmented across water utilities.
reasons.validity: The moment is thin: landlords rarely need a prior water bill to split a shared meter, and the named issuer is unlikely to sign roll membership.
reasons.coherence: Blind signing is odd here since the utility would need to know the roll membership anyway, and the stated tiny anonymity set undermines the privacy claim.
reasons.novelty: Utility-subsidy rolls are on the known list, though the landlord verifier and shared-meter angle is slightly new.
reasons.provenance: Unlinkability and blind issuance are generic ZK properties; the idea would read the same without citing them.
reasons.retention_law: Nothing suggests a landlord must retain the old bill, but this is not clearly established.
reasons.linkability: With a tiny eligible pool, membership itself identifies the tenant, so unlinkability gives little benefit.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: A public water utility has no obvious reason to build a signed roll credential for a landlord use case.
reasons.no_wallet: A landlord has little motivation to adopt a wallet flow when a bill photo works.

reasons.rubric: A time-windowed cleared boolean is a simple predicate with a hospital issuer, but frequency is medium and facilities may need paper records.
reasons.validity: Entry screening at care facilities and kindergartens is real, though a hospital signing a generic cleared status for visitors is a stretch.
reasons.coherence: The pieces fit well: validity window, hospital issuer and minimal disclosure, though the stated audit-retention weakness cuts against it.
reasons.novelty: Health-status clearance for facility entry is not on the known list and is a fresh moment.
reasons.provenance: The unlinkability borrowing is generic, and the HIPAA-style field stripping is not what the idea does; it would read the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: Facilities may be required by health authorities to keep specific records, which I cannot confirm.
reasons.linkability: Hospital-signed credentials with a short window can be unlinked from the visit, and the facility learns little.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals would need to issue a new attestation product and take liability for a clearance claim, which is not their usual role.
reasons.no_wallet: Facility staff at a door are used to paper slips, and a wallet scan adds friction.

reasons.rubric: A trip-count threshold is simple, but the issuer is an unwilling platform needing zkTLS, so it is more design-heavy and frequency is low.
reasons.validity: Gig drivers applying for fleet leases is real, but lessors mostly underwrite on earnings, so trip count alone is not sufficient for the decision.
reasons.coherence: The honest weakness that the lessor wants income contradicts the claim that experience alone suffices.
reasons.novelty: Gig-work experience for lease qualification is a new issuer and moment relative to the known list.
reasons.provenance: Differential privacy and census singling-out rules do not relate to a threshold proof over a trip log; the borrowings are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Lessors doing credit assessment may need to retain income evidence, which weakens the benefit, though this is unconfirmed.
reasons.linkability: A threshold proof over a portal session reveals little beyond the predicate and is reasonably unlinkable.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform did not agree to be an issuer and could block scraping, relying on zkTLS against its terms.
reasons.no_wallet: Driver and lessor both use phones, so a prover app is plausible, but a lessor still needs to adopt a verifier.

reasons.rubric: Per-drop uniqueness is a simple nullifier predicate with high-frequency use, but the telco ecosystem is fragmented and multi-line holders break one-person.
reasons.validity: Scalper accounts on ticketing and limited drops are a real Taiwanese problem, but a subscriber is not a person, so the predicate is only partly sufficient.
reasons.coherence: Telco-signed subscriber binding with a scoped pseudonym fits the stated goal, with honest limits acknowledged.
reasons.novelty: One-person-one-account is a known case via the brokerage nullifier, though limited-release retail and a telco issuer are new.
reasons.provenance: Narrowing the answer to duplicate or not matches the scoped nullifier, but the idea would read much the same without the registry analogy.
reasons.retention_law: Retailers have no stated duty to retain subscriber numbers for drops, though I cannot confirm sector rules.
reasons.linkability: A per-drop scoped pseudonym prevents cross-platform tracking while still catching repeats.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Carriers would have to build and sign an attestation service with no revenue case, which is a real obstacle.
reasons.no_wallet: Buyers on phones with an existing SMS flow are unlikely to adopt a wallet step for a small benefit.

reasons.rubric: A once-per-promotion uniqueness check is simple and frequent, but coupon value is low and the telco issuer ecosystem is fragmented.
reasons.validity: Promo abuse is real in delivery apps, but the idea itself concedes the business case is thin, and the coupon stakes do not justify telco involvement.
reasons.coherence: Parts fit, but it largely duplicates the previous idea with a lower-stakes verifier.
reasons.novelty: It is essentially the known Sybil nullifier case applied to a coupon, so a near rewording.
reasons.provenance: The deletion-on-purpose-lapse borrowing is a motivation for not collecting data, which the idea would argue anyway.
reasons.retention_law: No legal duty to hold the phone number for a promotion appears likely, though uncertain.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Telcos have little reason to sign uniqueness attestations for coupon farming.
reasons.no_wallet: Users claiming a few hundred NT dollars will not install a wallet when SMS works.

reasons.rubric: A same-person match across two issuers is a multi-source predicate with a fragmented university ecosystem, and subsidy offices may require the full ID.
reasons.validity: Student rentals near campuses are real, but a landlord seldom needs an enrolled-student guarantee and the subsidy office likely needs full identity.
reasons.coherence: The stated weakness that guarantors, addresses and full ID are still needed undermines the proposed replacement of the file.
reasons.novelty: Enrollment status appears in the scholarship case and tenancy in the rental case, so this mixes known moments with only a small new twist.
reasons.provenance: Narrowing to same person and unlinkability are both just inherent to the proposal; they are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Subsidy offices may legally require the full ID number, which blocks the benefit for that verifier.
reasons.linkability: Binding two credentials to the same holder can be done unlinkably, so this is not a major issue.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Universities issuing a wallet-bound enrollment credential is plausible but fragmented across schools.
reasons.no_wallet: Students are phone-native, though landlords still prefer photocopies.

reasons.rubric: A date-range boolean from a hospital is a simple predicate with high frequency, but the verifier may have a legal or adjudication need for the diagnosis.
reasons.validity: Diagnosis certificates over-disclose to HR and the moment is very common, but employer and insurer rules may require the original, so sufficiency is doubtful.
reasons.coherence: The attested fit-for-work window and the stated adoption dependence on rule changes are consistent.
reasons.novelty: Medical leave certification is not on the known list, so this is a fresh moment.
reasons.provenance: Selective disclosure from a whole credential is genuinely the mechanism, but the jury-confidentiality borrowing is decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Labour rules and insurers may require the diagnosis or original certificate, which I cannot confirm but which the idea itself flags.
reasons.linkability: A date-range boolean reveals little, though the issuing hospital identity itself can hint at the condition.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals already issue certificates, so a minimal variant is a plausible but non-trivial change.
reasons.no_wallet: HR and claims desks accept scans today and a wallet flow would need policy change.

reasons.rubric: A count-to-address predicate over a zkTLS portal is a complex multi-field proof from an unwilling issuer, and landlords prefer stronger documents.
reasons.validity: Landlords in Taiwan ask for leases, utility bills or household registration, and order history is easily gamed, so it is not sufficient for the decision.
reasons.coherence: The proof is self-described as weak and gameable, which clashes with its use as evidence of stable residence.
reasons.novelty: Proof of residence is on the known list via the renting case, but delivery-order history is a novel evidence source.
reasons.provenance: The narrow-answer analogy and scope-grant concern add nothing the proposal needs; decorative.
reasons.retention_law: A landlord has no apparent duty to retain order screenshots, though this is unconfirmed.
reasons.linkability: A count over an address can be shown without revealing items, but the address itself may link the tenant.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The platform never agreed to issue and the idea relies on scraping, which it could block.
reasons.no_wallet: Landlords and building committees will not adopt a verifier flow when a lease or utility bill is easy.
